frame: metres; +X east, +Y up, +Z south; origin at the centre of the Pyramid's base; ground level of the Cour Napoleon is y = 0. See coordinates.md.
portalRule: Portals are undirected passages. Each is listed on both rooms. `kind` is descriptive: door, passage, stair, arch, tunnel, open (no door leaf). Stairs connect different floorY values.

rooms.name: Hall Napoleon

dimensions.source: louvre.fr gives 2,500 m2 for private events in the hall; the documentary on the Grand Louvre gives a 9 m depth for '2,000 m2'. We hold the area at 2,500 and make the room 60 x 42 to sit under and around the 35.42 m pyramid.

ceiling.notes: Smooth white concrete tinted with dust of the same Chassagne stone as the walls; the four-sided underside of the pyramid opens through it.

rooms.lighting: Daylight falling through the glass pyramid, plus continuous cove light on the walls. Bright, cool, no spotlights.

portals.note: exit stairs up through the pyramid

rooms.name: Cour Napoleon

dimensions.source: Area 28,000 m2 is the Louvre's published figure; the 200 x 140 split is ours.

ceiling.notes: Paved court, no roof.

rooms.lighting: Full daylight. The pyramid and the three satellite pyramids cast the only shadows worth modelling.

rooms.name: Place du Carrousel

dimensions.source: Bounded by the Arc du Carrousel at its west end (220 m from the pyramid tip-to-tip on the axis) and the Cour Napoleon at its east. Not a separately published area.

rooms.lighting: Full daylight. Hedges screen the inverted pyramid's centre (it is not visible from the surface).

rooms.name: Denon approach, under the court

dimensions.source: Reconstructed undercroft under the Cour Napoleon's southern half. It spans from the Hall Napoleon's east wall (x = 30) to the Daru staircase's south face (z = 70.5) so that both doors sit on shared walls rather than on a corner.

ceiling.notes: White concrete with slot lights.

rooms.lighting: Artificial, warm white, low level; a bright band at the far end where the Daru staircase begins.

rooms.name: Richelieu link, under the court

dimensions.source: Rises from the Hall Napoleon (-9) to the courtyard level (0). In reality the Passage Richelieu is a ramp at courtyard level.

rooms.lighting: Artificial; daylit slot at the courtyard end.

rooms.name: Daru Staircase (Escalier Daru), with the landing of the Winged Victory
rooms.nameFr: Escalier Daru, palier de la Victoire de Samothrace

dimensions.source: No published survey. Its south face starts on the Denon wing's own building line (z = 70.5) so that the undercroft arrives at a wall rather than a corner; sized so the 5.57 m Samothrace monument sits at the head of three flights with 5 m of clearance above it and 8 m of open landing around it.

ceiling.notes: Renaissance-style coffered ceiling above the top landing; the lower flights are open to the courtyard wall.

rooms.lighting: From above, through high windows; the Nike is raked from the upper left and lit from below only faintly.

rooms.name: Michelangelo Gallery

dimensions.source: Plan footprint is ours; the room number and the three sculptures are the Louvre's.

ceiling.notes: Flat plaster vault between stone ribs, painted off-white.

rooms.lighting: Cool daylight from high side windows plus a top light; sculpture on low plinths, shadows short and soft.

rooms.name: Salle Daru (Roman red room)

dimensions.source: No published area. Deep enough for the 6.21 x 9.79 m Coronation on the long wall with 4 m of hanging clearance.

ceiling.notes: Lefuel's top-lit salles: a flat glazed strip over the centre of the room, cornice at 7.5 m.

rooms.lighting: Diffuse top light, no visible source; the red walls take the light down and the gilded frames catch it.

rooms.name: Salle Denon

dimensions.source: As Salle Daru.

ceiling.notes: Same Lefuel strip light.

rooms.lighting: As Salle Daru.

rooms.name: Salle Mollien (Roman red room)

dimensions.source: As Salle Daru.

ceiling.notes: Same Lefuel strip light.

rooms.lighting: As Salle Daru.

rooms.name: Salle des Etats (Mona Lisa room)

dimensions.source: Louvre press (2019): 698 m2 of floor. Length 40 m is the widely quoted figure; width follows from the area.

ceiling.notes: Glass ceiling added in the Third Republic so that no reflection falls on the paintings; a lantern-like strip over the whole room.

rooms.lighting: Cool diffuse top light; the Mona Lisa in her own glass case is separately lit, brighter than the room, sitting alone on a free-standing cimaise.

rooms.name: Sessions gallery (reconstructed link)

dimensions.source: EXPLICITLY INVENTED. The real museum links the Salle des Etats to the Grande Galerie through the Escalier Mollien and the Salle des Sessions, a set of spaces we do not model. This single gallery stands in for them and is the only room in the route with no real counterpart.

rooms.lighting: Top light, dimmer than the Salles Rouges, so the Grande Galerie reads as the bright release.

rooms.name: Grande Galerie

dimensions.source: Width 13 m and museum-room length 288 m are both published. The 288 m includes the Salon Carre bay, which we model separately, so the open run here is 268 m.

ceiling.notes: The 1990s/2000s glazed roof: a continuous lantern running the whole length, with transverse ribs every 5.5 m.

rooms.lighting: Even, seamless top light for 268 m. No windows on the river side. This is the brightest and flattest light in the building.

rooms.name: Salon Carre

dimensions.source: The square salon at the east end of the Grande Galerie; its 20 m side is our estimate from the Grande Galerie's 288 m including it.

ceiling.notes: Coved, with the glazed lantern continuing in.

rooms.lighting: Top light plus daylight from the east, because the room turns the corner toward the Petite Galerie.

rooms.name: Rotonde d'Apollon

dimensions.source: Circular in reality; modelled as the square of its bounding footprint, to be cut to a cylinder by the builder.

ceiling.notes: Barrel vault entirely gilded, with Delacroix's Apollo Slays Python in the central panel and Le Brun's Hours around it; gilded stucco reliefs on the coves. The vault crown sits at y = 20.85 m, which is 13.85 m above this floor. The Louvre also publishes a 15 m ceiling; the two figures cannot both be measured from the same floor, and the crown is the one that must not be breached, so it is the one we hold.

rooms.lighting: Dim, warm; a lantern above.

rooms.name: Galerie d'Apollon

dimensions.source: Louvre press office: 61.34 m long, 15 m ceiling. Width is our estimate to fit the 23.75 m deep Petite Galerie wing.

ceiling.notes: Barrel vault entirely gilded, with Delacroix's Apollo Slays Python in the central panel and Le Brun's Hours around it; gilded stucco reliefs on the coves. The vault crown sits at y = 20.85 m, which is 13.85 m above this floor. The Louvre also publishes a 15 m ceiling; the two figures cannot both be measured from the same floor, and the crown is the one that must not be breached, so it is the one we hold.

rooms.lighting: The most dramatic interior light in the palace: narrow high windows on one side throw raking light across the gold, and the vault glows rather than being lit.

rooms.name: Pavillon de l'Horloge

dimensions.source: Roof frame measured at 21.50 x 16.50 m between wall plates (Goutal/GeneB, 2017); the pavilion's masonry block is wider, and we take the full wing depth 23.75 m and a 28 m frontage.

ceiling.notes: Stone vaults at each level; the Salle de la Chapelle was originally 12.1 m high and double-height (Blavette restoration survey). Modelled here as one continuous 20 m volume.

rooms.lighting: Daylight through the east and west arches; deep and cool. The clock face is lit from inside at dusk.

rooms.name: Henri II Staircase

dimensions.source: The straight-flight stone stair in the Lescot wing. Sized to the wing depth.

ceiling.notes: Stone barrel vault with carved coffers.

rooms.lighting: One tall window at the half-landing; the stair reads as a shaft of light in a stone box.

rooms.name: Salle des Caryatides

dimensions.source: Wikipedia FR (citing the Louvre): a majestic hall of 600 m2. Split 25 x 23.75 to fill the Lescot wing depth. A popular guide's 30 x 13 m is inconsistent with 600 m2 and is rejected.

ceiling.notes: The oldest surviving coffered ceiling in the Louvre: deep stone beams on the walls, five bays, painted and gilded in the 16th-century manner.

rooms.lighting: Daylight from the courtyard side, low and raking; the room is stone-cold in colour and reads as shadowed even at noon.

rooms.name: Rotonde de Mars (threshold to the Petite Galerie)

dimensions.source: Real wing volume at the south-west corner of the ring, measured only through the 23.75 m wing depth and the 160 / 112.5 m square. The rotunda itself exists; its use here as the sole threshold between the Caryatides, room 346 and the Galerie d'Apollon is our reconstruction, and it holds the only stair from the ground floor up to the Petite Galerie's 7 m gallery floor.

ceiling.notes: Domed in reality. Modelled as a shallow stone dome over a half-landing, with the stair to level 1 rising in its south half.

rooms.lighting: Lit only from the gallery door above and the two ground-floor doors, so it is the darkest room in the ring. Its job is to make the turn from the Renaissance rooms up to the gold of the Petite Galerie feel like a climb.

portals.note: up 7 m at the south end

rooms.name: Greek antiquities, classical and Hellenistic

dimensions.source: Wing depth 23.75 m; length set by the Cour Carree's 160 m square split into three south-wing rooms.

ceiling.notes: Flat plaster with a deep cove; the room is a 19th-century sculpture gallery.

rooms.lighting: High side windows on the court side, so figures are lit from above and to one side; the floor stays dim.

rooms.name: Venus de Milo room (classical and Hellenistic Greek art)
rooms.nameFr: Salle de la Venus de Milo

dimensions.source: As room 346. The Louvre's own trail says you reach the Venus 'between the red marble pillars', which sets the room's trim.

rooms.lighting: A single top light over the plinth plus low side light; the figure stands free of the wall so it is lit from three sides.

rooms.name: Crypt of the Sphinx

dimensions.source: As room 346. Sources disagree on the level: the Louvre collection pages list room 338 at Niveau 0, some guides say -1. We follow the collection pages and put it at 0.

ceiling.notes: Low stone vault on square piers; deliberately oppressive.

rooms.lighting: Very low ambient, a tight pool of light over the sphinx and faint uplight on the walls. Almost nothing else is visible.

rooms.name: Cour Carree

dimensions.source: A cited survey gives the court as 'un carre de 112,5 metres de cote'. Wikipedia's 160 m refers to the square formed by the buildings, outer face to outer face, which agrees: 112.5 + 2 x 23.75 = 160.

ceiling.notes: Walls rise 20.4 m to the cornice, then mansard roofs to about 29 m.

rooms.lighting: Open sky; the court is a light well for all four wings.

rooms.name: Colonnade gallery (inside Perrault's east wing)

dimensions.source: Wing depth from the 160-112.5 relationship. The 183 m Colonnade façade extends 11.5 m beyond the court on each side; that surplus volume belongs to the exterior zone.

rooms.lighting: The two-storey order keeps the room in deep shade behind the columns; light comes in horizontal bars between them.

rooms.name: Sully level 2, north corridor

dimensions.source: Circulation invented for the replica to reach the Dutch rooms on level 2 without modelling the whole Lemercier wing. Its footprint is real wing volume; its use as one corridor is ours.

rooms.lighting: Windows on the court side only; intermittent bands of daylight.

rooms.name: Dutch Golden Age rooms

dimensions.source: Wing depth; room numbers 837-838 are the Louvre's current location for the two Vermeers.

ceiling.notes: Small-scale rooms: low ceilings, top light through a small lantern.

rooms.lighting: Dim and intimate. The Lacemaker hangs in a case and is lit to a much higher level than the room, so it appears to float.

rooms.name: Passage Richelieu

dimensions.source: The real passage runs under the Pavillon de la Bibliotheque between the Cour Puget and the Cour Marly. Its 14 m width is our estimate.

ceiling.notes: Stone soffit; daylight slots.

rooms.lighting: A long shaded slot between two sunlit courts; the end of the passage glows.

rooms.name: Cour Marly

dimensions.source: Glazed roof 57.05 x 42.61 m (the structural record); internal north-south width 41 m at the west end (Arup). Floor 54 x 41 is inset from the roof by the cornice propping.

ceiling.notes: Pei/Macary shallow vault on steel tubes, propped off the old cornices, 7 m of rise above the cornice line and no higher, so it stays behind the Rivoli roofline. The vault apex is estimated at 26.4 m above the courtyard, about 6 m over the 20.4 m cornice, which is the structural record's stated limit for the whole glazing scheme.

rooms.lighting: The best daylight in the museum: a bright diffuse sky over the whole court, terraced so the Marly Horses at the top catch it and the lower terrace stays in soft shadow.

rooms.name: Cour Puget

dimensions.source: Arup: north-south internal width falls from over 41 m at Marly's west end to under 28 m at Khorsabad's east, so Puget sits between and we hold 41 m for it. Floor is three terraced levels; the Louvre labels the room Level -1.

ceiling.notes: Same vault system as Marly, with openable smoke vents under the eaves. The vault apex is estimated at 26.4 m above the courtyard, about 6 m over the 20.4 m cornice, which is the structural record's stated limit for the whole glazing scheme.

rooms.lighting: Diffuse from above; the terraces create a shaft that keeps the lower level in cool shade — the intended contrast with Marly.

rooms.name: Cour Khorsabad

dimensions.source: Arup puts the east end at under 28 m north-south; the Louvre names the room 229 (Elae Omidyar - Mir-Djalali). 32 m is the smallest consistent footprint for four lamassu of 4.36 m plus circulation.

ceiling.notes: Third of Pei's three courts; the roof here is lower than Marly's. The vault apex is estimated at 24.0 m above the courtyard, about 6 m over the 20.4 m cornice, which is the structural record's stated limit for the whole glazing scheme.

rooms.lighting: Cool and even, the opposite of the Egyptian crypt. The gypsum alabaster of the bulls is almost white against the slate walls.

rooms.name: Room of the Code of Hammurabi

dimensions.source: Mesopotamian rooms are small and dense; the footprint is ours, the room number is the Louvre's.

rooms.lighting: Spotlit from above front, everything else dark; the black basalt stele needs a single hard light to show the cuneiform.

rooms.name: Richelieu staircase

dimensions.source: The Richelieu wing's stair, modelled as a flight rising over the north end of the Passage Richelieu, which is how such stairs sit in this building. Its plan and its level numbering are ours.

ceiling.notes: Stone vault with an open well, over the passage below.

rooms.lighting: Top light down the well.

rooms.name: Napoleon III Apartments, Grand Salon

dimensions.source: No published dimensions for the salon. 30 x 19 m matches the wing's Rivoli range depth and reads correctly against photographs of the room.

ceiling.notes: Painted and gilded coffered ceiling with a central light, hung with a crystal chandelier.

rooms.lighting: Chandelier and wall sconces only, all warm; the most golden room in the palace and the only one that is better at night than by day.

route.note: Approach across the Cour Napoleon; the pyramid is the entrance.
Down the spiral stair under the pyramid.
East under the court.
Up three flights; the Winged Victory stands at the top landing and is visible from the first step.
Coronation on the long wall; Grande Odalisque and Horatii flanking.
Pass-through: the transition between the David and Delacroix hang.
Raft of the Medusa, Liberty, Sardanapalus: the three largest Romantic canvases.
Mona Lisa free-standing opposite the Wedding at Cana.
Reconstructed link; turn south toward the river.
Walk east down 268 m of top-lit Italian painting.
Turn north; the gallery ends.
Threshold of the Apollo gallery.
61 m of gold; the crown jewels in wall cases on the left.
Down the corner stair to the ground floor: the only way out of the Petite Galerie. Dark stone after all that gold.
Out through the clock pavilion to the Cour Carree, having come back along the Caryatides.
Cross the court toward Perrault's colonnade, then return.
Behind the coupled columns.
Down into the Renaissance wing.
Diana of Versailles and the Borghese Gladiator among Roman marbles.
South wing, Greek classical.
The Venus stands free, in the middle of the room.
Optional spur: the pink granite sphinx in near darkness.
Out through the clock pavilion to the Cour Carree, having come back along the Caryatides.
Down and north under the Cour Napoleon.
Between the two sculpture courts.
The Marly Horses on the top terrace under the glass vault.
Down one terrace; Milo of Croton.
The lamassu in the third court.
The stele, spotlit.
Up behind the north range.
End in crimson and gold under a chandelier.

omissions: Sully level -1 (medieval Louvre moat, Louvre history rooms) and level 2 apart from the Dutch rooms.
Denon Egyptian galleries, the Cour du Sphinx, and Cour Lefueil in the middle of the Denon wing.
Richelieu level 2 (Northern schools, Rubens Medici cycle) and the whole Aile de Rohan / Aile de Marsan / Pavillon de Marsan, which is now the Musee des Arts Decoratifs.
The Salle des Sept Chefs, the Escalier Mollien and the Salle des Sessions; the invented galerie-des-sessions stands in for them.
All of the museum west of the Pavillon de Flore and east of the Colonnade.
